insights.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6 of 8 targets for 84 yards in the Seahawks' Week 18 win against the Niners.
insights.sub_note: Most of his production came against Renardo Green, where he was targeted 7 times across 10 matchups, hauling in 5 receptions for 67 yards, the most receptions and yards Green has given up to a player in his career.

insights.title: The 49ers offense generated -0.46 EPA per play in their Week 18 loss to the Seahawks, their lowest mark of the season, while posting a 40.5% success rate, their 3rd-lowest this season.
insights.sub_note: Christian McCaffrey was limited to 23 yards on eight carries, recording a 25.0% success rate, his 2nd-lowest of the season, and failed to force a missed tackle on rushing for the first time in a game since Week 12 of 2022 (min. 8 carries).

insights.title: Zach Charbonnet forced a career-high 10 missed tackles, while Kenneth Walker III forced 7 missed tackles.
insights.sub_note: The two Seahawks' backs combined to gain 74 yards due to missed tackles. Overall, the 49ers defense missed 21 tackles, the 2nd-most by a defense in a game this season.

insights.title: Brock Purdy faced pressure on just 34.4% of dropbacks against the Seahawks, a significant drop from their Week 1 matchup (60.5%).
insights.sub_note: When under pressure, Purdy completed 3 of 7 passes for 25 yards, compared to 16 of 20 for 102 yards and his lone interception when not under pressure. Purdy attempted no deep passes in the game, marking his only contest this season without a deep attempt. Instead, he passed under 10 air yards on 74.1% of his attempts, completing 15 of 20 such passes for 65 yards and an interception.

insights.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has recorded a league-high 33 receptions for 546 yards against Cover 4 this season, with his yardage total nearly twice that of any other player this season (Puka Nacua, 277) and almost 200 yards more than any player in the last eight seasons.
insights.sub_note: His 44.6% target rate and 5.4 yards per route against Cover 4 are both the highest marks of any player since 2018 (min. 50 routes). The 49ers have played Cover 4 at the 5th-highest rate in the NFL this season (25.5%) and have allowed 9.0 yards per target to wide receivers (5th-most). They have allowed 19.3 PPG in eight games in which they have played Cover 4 at a rate above 25%, compared to 25.5 in eight games when they have not done so.

insights.title: The 49ers have used 21 personnel 375 times this season, featuring Kyle Juszczyk on 373 of those plays, while no other offense has done so more than 222 times.
insights.sub_note: They have recorded at least 200 yards from 21 personnel in each of their last three games – no other team has done so all season – averaging 7.2 yards per play and scoring 6 touchdowns from 21 in that span. The Seahawks have matched 21 with nickel on a league-high 94.1% of snaps facing the grouping this season, while the rest of the NFL has used base on 59.4% of plays against 21. They have allowed 3.8 yards per play (6th-fewest) in nickel against 21 and have allowed 4.8 yards per play (4th-fewest) on a league-high 784 plays in nickel overall.

insights.title: Sam Darnold has the highest passer rating in the NFL (115.5) on throws from outside the pocket this season (min. 20 such attempts), with Brock Purdy's 111.4 mark being the 3rd-highest.
insights.sub_note: Darnold has completed a league-high 62.0% of such passes, while Purdy has completed 11 of 15 such passes for 132 yards and a league-high 4 touchdowns since the 49ers' Week 14 bye.

insights.title: Ricky Pearsall led the NFL with 264 receiving yards on downfield throws through Week 1 to Week 3 before leaving Week 4 with an injury.
insights.sub_note: After catching just one downfield pass for 13 yards on five targets from Weeks 11-13, he has caught all 7 of his downfield targets for 141 yards in his last two games in Week 15 vs the Titans and Week 17 vs the Bears.

insights.title: On 734 offensive plays with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the field this season, the Seahawks have averaged 6.6 yards per play.
insights.sub_note: With Smith-Njigba on the bench (214 plays) they have gained just 3.6 yards per play. The 3.0-yard split is the largest among all wide receivers this season (min. 50 plays on and off) by half a yard.

insights.title: Bryce Huff has generated more than twice as many pressures (46) and quick pressures (19) as any other 49ers defender this season despite missing two games.
insights.sub_note: The next-closest 49ers in quick pressures are Nick Bosa (7), who hasn't played since the first quarter of Week 3, and slot cornerback Upton Stout (7). Clelin Ferrell is tied with Huff for the most sacks on the team (4.0) despite having rushed the passer just 130 times (9th-most on the team) this season.

insights.title: The Seahawks have converted tackles effectively in the run game, missing 11.6% of their tackles on designed runs, the 2nd-lowest rate in the NFL.
insights.sub_note: They have allowed explosive plays of 10+ yards on 5.3% of designed runs, the lowest rate in the league and 2nd-lowest by any team since 2016. The Seahawks have allowed such rushers to gain an average of 2.2 yards after hitting them behind the line of scrimmage, the fewest by any defense since the 2020 Saints. No other team this season has allowed fewer than 2.7 yards on average following contact behind the line.

insights.title: Brock Purdy is one of just two quarterbacks to average a time to throw of 3+ seconds this season – his 3.19-second mark is quicker than that of only Caleb Williams (3.21 seconds).
insights.sub_note: Since the 49ers' Week 14 bye, Purdy has the league's highest passer rating (136.9) by almost 20 points on throws longer than 2.5 seconds, throwing 9 touchdowns and 0 interceptions.

insights.title: Sam Darnold has turned the ball over on 7.8% of his pressured dropbacks this season, the highest rate among qualified quarterbacks.
insights.sub_note: Despite being pressured on only 29.0% of his dropbacks (5th-lowest), Darnold has thrown 6 interceptions (T-4th-most) and lost 5 fumbles on strip sacks (2nd-most) when under pressure this season. He has lost -255.5 percentage points of win probability when pressured, the 2nd-most in the NFL behind only Jalen Hurts (-291.3%).

insights.title: Christian McCaffrey has forced a league-high 112 missed tackles this season, 10 more than any other player.
insights.sub_note: McCaffrey's mark is already the 3rd most of any player in the last 10 years, trailing only Bijan Robinson (115 in 2024) and Derrick Henry (121 in 2020). His 112 rushing yards after contact in Week 17 against the Bears was his most since Week 2 of 2023.

insights.title: Sam Darnold has faced five or more pass rushers on 35.7% of his dropbacks this season, the 3rd-highest rate among qualified quarterbacks.
insights.sub_note: While Darnold has thrown a league-high 7 interceptions against the blitz this season, he has averaged the 2nd-most yards per attempt (8.9) and the 4th-highest success rate (51.7%) on blitzed dropbacks. The 49ers have blitzed at the 4th-lowest rate in the NFL this season (22.4%) and have generated pressure at a 35.6% rate when blitzing compared to 23.5% with four rushers or fewer.

insights.title: Robert Saleh-led defenses played Cover 4 at a top 3 rate in the NFL in every full season he coached from 2019 to 2024, but the 2025 team temporarily abandoned the coverage following Fred Warner's injury (12.9% usage in Weeks 6-10).
insights.sub_note: They have also shown a decline in usage of Cover 4 in each of their last four games, culminating in a 15.2% mark in Week 17, while opting for Cover 3 on a season-high 54.3% of opponent dropbacks in that contest. They have additionally produced strong results in man coverage (2.9 yards per dropback allowed, 2nd-fewest in NFL) since Week 12.

insights.title: Since the Seahawks bye week (Week 8), Zach Charbonnet has gained 4.3 yards after contact per carry, the 2nd-most mark among running backs during that span (min. 50 carries).
insights.sub_note: Additionally, Charbonnet (30.5%, 4th-highest) and Kenneth Walker III (30.0%, 6th) are one of two RB duos (Croskey-Merritt and Rodriguez Jr.) to force missed tackle rates of 30% or higher during that span.

insights.title: The 49ers defense has felt the effects of Fred Warner's injury, allowing 6.8 yards per dropback (6th-most) since Week 6 when they lost him in the first quarter, compared to 5.9 yards per dropback (11th-fewest) from Weeks 1-5 with Warner healthy.
insights.sub_note: In the run game, they have stuffed 12.3% of rushers (4th-lowest) for loss or no gain since losing Warner after generating a 21.2% stuff rate (4th-highest) in the first five weeks.

insights.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has generated +291 receiving yards over expected on vertical routes this season, the most by any receiver in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016).
insights.sub_note: Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 696 yards on vertical routes, while his 7 touchdowns on such routes are the 2nd-most behind only Davante Adams (10). His efficiency has been equally impressive, averaging 18.3 yards per target on vertical routes, the 2nd-highest mark among receivers with 25+ targets.

insights.title: The 49ers have 3 of the 10 defensive tackles with the lowest pressure rate generated this season (min. 200 pass rushes) in Kalia Davis (3.0%, 3rd-lowest), Alfred Collins (3.8%, 8th-lowest), and Jordan Elliott (4.2%, 9th lowest).
insights.sub_note: No other team has more than one defensive tackle in the bottom 10.

insights.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has totaled 686 receiving yards on play action targets this season, over 200 more than any other player, and leads the NFL with 6 touchdowns.
insights.sub_note: His 5.8 yards per route off play action are the most since A.J. Green in 2016 (min. 50 routes); Smith-Njigba has been targeted on 32.2% of his play action routes, compared to Green's 49.4% mark.

insights.title: Dee Winters has been targeted 88 times this season, at least 10 more than all but one other linebacker (Devin White, 89).
insights.sub_note: However, his 4.9 yards per target allowed is the 2nd-fewest among linebackers with 40+ targets. Since the 49ers' Week 14 bye, he's allowed just 40 yards in coverage on 14 targets, including a pick-6 in Week 16 against the Colts. Winters became the only inside linebacker this season to eclipse 20 mph as a ball carrier on that play, reaching 20.15 mph.

insights.title: Each of the three Seahawks offensive linemen who played at least 100 snaps in 2024 has decreased their pressure rate allowed by a factor of at least 30% in 2025.
insights.sub_note: LT Charles Cross allowed an 11.5% pressure rate (31st/35 LT, min. 200 pass blocks) in 2024 and has lowered his rate to 7.2% (6th/34 LT) in 2025. RG Anthony Bradford has decreased from 9.5% (30th/36 RG) to 6.0% (8th/33) this season. RT Abraham Lucas has lowered his mark from 9.8% (25th/37 RT) to 6.6% (7th/39) this season. LG Grey Zabel (5.7% pressure rate, 8th/35 LG) has also helped author the offensive line turnaround.

insights.title: Deommodore Lenoir has been targeted at the lowest rate of any outside cornerback this season (9.8%, min. 250 coverage snaps).
insights.sub_note: Lenoir has allowed 0.7 yards per coverage snap, the 8th-fewest among the same group. In his last two games, while Renardo Green has been out of the lineup, Lenoir has been targeted just 3 times on 82 coverage snaps (3.7%) and has allowed two receptions for 35 yards.

insights.title: Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams have combined for 88 pressures this season, the most by a defensive tackle duo in the NFL.
insights.sub_note: They have each generated 44 pressures this season, tied for the 7th-most among defensive tackles. Murphy and Williams are the only interior duo to both rank in the top 10 in pressures among defensive tackles since 2023.

insights.title: Since returning from injury in Week 11, Brock Purdy has accumulated 298 total yards on extended dropbacks (4+ seconds), trailing only Justin Herbert (383) during that span.
insights.sub_note: Purdy has 241 passing yards (3rd-most) and 57 scramble rush yards (10th) since Week 11. The Seahawks defense has allowed the 5th-most total yards on extended dropbacks this season. However, on such dropbacks, they have been better at limiting scramble rush yards (111, 10th-fewest) compared to passing yards (492, 5th-most).

insights.title: Nick Emmanwori is the only player in the NFL that has aligned at both linebacker (37.6%) and slot corner (45.8%) on over 35.0% of his snaps this season.
insights.sub_note: He has recorded 65 tackles from such alignments, the 2nd-most among defensive backs, while missing just 6 tackles (8.5%), the 4th-lowest missed tackle rate among DBs with 40+ tackle attempts from LB/slot.

insights.title: Brock Purdy has completed 60.2% of his passes beyond 10 air yards this season, the 2nd-highest mark in the NFL.
insights.sub_note: Since the Week 14 bye, his 148.5 passer rating on such throws leads the league, and his 534 yards trail only Matthew Stafford (659).

insights.title: The Seahawks defense has generated the 4th-highest pressure rate in the NFL this season (39.1%) despite blitzing at the 8th-lowest rate (22.9%).
insights.sub_note: They are one of just two teams (Broncos) to have generated a top 5 pressure rate both when rushing 4 or fewer (36.4%, 4th-highest) and when blitzing (48.0%, 4th-highest).

insights.title: On third and fourth downs this season, Brock Purdy has released the ball in under 2.5 seconds on 33.3% of his attempts, the 2nd-lowest rate in the NFL; Mac Jones has done so at a 51.9% rate (4th-highest).
insights.sub_note: However, Purdy has completed 24 of his 25 quick passes on late downs for 243 yards and 3 touchdowns, generating a 96.0% completion percentage, the only time since at least 2016 a qualified quarterback has reached 90%. Jones, meanwhile, has completed 20 of 40 such passes for 228 yards, 2 touchdowns, and 2 interceptions for an NFL-low 50.0% completion percentage.

insights.title: While the Seahawks do not have a player in the top 20 in total pressures this season, they have a league-high 5 players with 40+ pressures; no other team has more than 3.
insights.sub_note: Their top four edge rushers – DeMarcus Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu, Boye Mafe, and Derick Hall – are the only group of four edge teammates to rush the passer at least 225 times apiece. All have a pressure rate above 13%, placing each of them in the top 32 among 85 edge rushers with 200+ pass rushes.

insights.title: Christian McCaffrey leads all running backs this season with 890 receiving yards and 7 touchdowns.
insights.sub_note: Most of his production has come from the backfield, where he leads all running backs with 662 yards and 5 touchdowns (T-most). His 662 such yards are already the 5th-most of any player in the last 10 seasons, and the top 2 marks both belong to McCaffrey (2018 and 2019). He also has 166 receiving yards (2nd most) and 2 touchdowns (T-most) from the slot.

insights.title: Drake Thomas has allowed a 58.3% completion percentage in coverage this season, the 3rd-lowest among 67 linebackers targeted at least 25 times.
insights.sub_note: He has not allowed a touchdown on his 48 targets, the 8th-most targets of any player without a TD. As such, his 74.7 passer rating allowed is the 6th-lowest among those linebackers, while teammate Ernest Jones ranks 4th with a 70.2 passer rating allowed, owing heavily to his position-lead-tying 5 interceptions.

insights.title: The 49ers (65.6%) and Seahawks (55.8%) have used condensed formations (total width below 20 yards) at the highest and 2nd-highest rates, respectively, in the NFL this season.
insights.sub_note: The 49ers' 65.6% rate is the highest of any team in at least the last 10 seasons. Since their Week 14 bye, the 49ers have used condensed formations on 77.1% of snaps, averaging +0.24 EPA per play (3rd-most) when doing so and scoring 42.3 PPG in that three-game span.

insights.title: The Seahawks' defensive backs have combined for 38 pressures this season, the most by any team's DB room.
insights.sub_note: Their 30.2% pressure rate ranks 3rd-highest. Nick Emmanwori has generated 15 pressures, the 2nd-most among defensive backs, while Ty Okada (46.7%) and Devon Witherspoon (42.9%) are two of just four DBs with at least 15 pass rushes to generate pressure rates north of 40%.

insights.title: Despite missing 6 games this season, George Kittle leads all tight ends with +156 receiving yards over expected.
insights.sub_note: 49ers quarterbacks have a perfect 158.3 passer rating when targeting him on throws of 10+ air yards this season; he is tied for the 3rd-most downfield touchdowns (4) and has totaled the 9th-most downfield yards (289). Since the start of 2023, his 1,487 receiving yards on downfield passes are almost 400 yards more than the next-closest TE (Travis Kelce, 1,121).

insights.title: The Seahawks have played cloud coverage at the 4th-highest rate entering Week 18 (32.1%).
insights.sub_note: In such coverage, the Seahawks have recorded 7 interceptions and have not allowed a touchdown; they have the most snaps in cloud coverage among teams who have not allowed a touchdown this season. Brock Purdy has averaged 8.9 yards per attempt when facing cloud coverage this season, the 5th-highest mark among qualified quarterbacks.

insights.title: Kyle Juszczyk has gone in motion on 47.2% of his snaps this season, the 2nd-highest rate among all players with 150+ offensive snaps.
insights.sub_note: He has been in motion when the snap occurs on 33.5% of plays, the 2nd-highest rate among the same group. Juszczyk has played 470 total snaps this season, almost 150 more than any other fullback.

insights.title: Devon Witherspoon has aligned as an outside cornerback on a career-high 56.9% of his snaps this season.
insights.sub_note: When playing outside, Witherspoon has been targeted at a 9.8% rate (3rd-lowest, min. 150 outside coverage snaps) and allowed 0.6 yards per snap, the 2nd-fewest among that group of corners behind only teammate Riq Woolen.

insights.title: Austen Pleasants allowed 4 pressures and a sack on 37 pass blocks (10.8%) filling in for an injured Trent Williams in Week 17.
insights.sub_note: Through the first three quarters, Pleasants allowed just one pressure (4.60-second time to pressure) on 27 pass blocks, but he allowed 3 pressures on 10 pass blocks in the fourth quarter. Williams allowed 10 pressures in Week 1 against the Seahawks, the most he’s allowed in any game since at least 2018.

insights.title: Riq Woolen has been targeted on 11.7% of his coverage snaps this season, the 5th-lowest mark among outside cornerbacks with at least 250 snaps in coverage.
insights.sub_note: In a related phenomenon, Woolen has allowed the fewest yards per snap among that group of corners (0.6). He has allowed just a 27.6% completion percentage in man coverage, the lowest by any defender to face 20+ targets in man since at least 2018, ceding 73 yards on 29 targets (2.5 per target).

insights.title: The 49ers have used nickel personnel on a league-high 79.8% of snaps this season, leading the next-closest team (Seahawks, 76.6%) by over 3 percentage points.
insights.sub_note: When facing 12 personnel, their 66.3% nickel rate is the 4th-highest mark in the league, while the Seahawks (82.4%) use nickel at the highest rate in the NFL against 12.

insights.title: The Seahawks have averaged 7.7 yards per play out of 12 personnel this season, the most by any offense since the 2018 Seahawks (7.8).
insights.sub_note: While they have used 12 personnel at the 11th-highest rate this season (27.2%), their overall reliance on heavier groupings extends further – they have used two or more tight ends or running backs on 57.4% of plays this season, trailing only the 49ers (57.4%) and Ravens (69.5%). With multiple RB or TE on the field, they have averaged a league-leading 6.0 yards per play.

insights.title: Since their bye week, the 49ers have alternated Upton Stout in a 'little nickel' grouping and Jason Pinnock in a 'big nickel' grouping.
insights.sub_note: When Stout got injured in Week 17, the 49ers kept the same rotation with Chase Lucas taking Stout's spot. The 49ers have used their nickel defense on 148 plays in that span, with Stout playing 97 snaps, Pinnock playing 27, and Lucas playing 24. None of the three have shared the field in a nickel grouping.

insights.title: In Week 1 against the 49ers, Jaxon Smith-Njigba was targeted on a career-high 61.9% of his routes (13 of 21), accounting for 91.0% of the Seahawks' air yards, the 8th-highest air yards share by a receiver in a game since at least 2016.
insights.sub_note: Smith-Njigba recorded 101 of his team-high 124 yards on vertical routes. He recorded at least 1 reception against 6 different 49ers defenders but matched up most frequently against Renardo Green, hauling in 2 of 4 targets for 51 yards across 7 matchups.

insights.title: In Week 1 against the Seahawks, Christian McCaffrey was targeted on 37.0% of his routes (10 of 27), his 3rd-highest target rate in a game this season.
insights.sub_note: McCaffery finished with 9 receptions for 73 yards, while gaining 63 yards after the catch, his 3rd-most in a game this season. However, he was not productive on the ground, getting stuffed at or behind the line of scrimmage a season-high 6 times. He averaged 3.1 yards per carry and forced a missed tackle rate of 18.6%, his 2nd-lowest in a game this season.

insights.title: In Week 1 against the 49ers, Sam Darnold completed 10 of his 12 short pass attempts (under 10 air yards) but generated only 22 yards, averaging a mere 1.8 yards per attempt.
insights.sub_note: Darnold found significantly more success pushing the ball downfield, completing 6 of 10 passes that traveled over 10 air yards for 128 yards.

insights.title: In Week 1 against the Seahawks, Brock Purdy was pressured on 60.5% of his dropbacks, the 4th-highest pressure rate faced by a qualified quarterback in a game this season and the highest in his career.
insights.sub_note: When under pressure, Purdy completed 13 of 20 passes for 126 yards and 1 touchdown but threw 2 interceptions.
